query: SELECT label, COUNT(*) FROM molecule GROUP BY label
result: symbol '+' occurs on 152 molecules and symbol '-' occurs on 191 molecules; 343 labelled molecules in total, no other label value and no null label
validation_method: value-domain enumeration over the molecule relation

query: SELECT DISTINCT element FROM atom; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom WHERE element <> lower(element)
result: 21 distinct lowercase chemical symbols: b, br, c, ca, cl, cu, f, h, i, k, n, na, o, p, pb, s, si, sn, te, y, zn; zero rows store a non-lowercase value
validation_method: distinct-value enumeration plus case check over the atom relation

query: SELECT bond_type, COUNT(*) FROM bond GROUP BY bond_type ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
result: '-' 10528 bonds, '=' 1844 bonds, '#' 6 bonds, and one bond (TR345_7_10) with no bond type recorded
validation_method: value-domain enumeration over the bond relation

query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) FROM atom; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM molecule; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) FROM atom WHERE molecule_id NOT IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM molecule)
result: 444 distinct molecules carry atoms, while the molecule relation holds 343 rows; 101 molecules that carry atoms and bonds have no molecule record and therefore no label; no molecule record lacks atoms
validation_method: set comparison between the molecule relation and the molecules referenced by atoms and bonds

query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT bond_id) FROM connected; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM connected c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected c2 WHERE c2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 AND c2.atom_id2 = c.atom_id AND c2.bond_id = c.bond_id)
result: 24758 rows over 12379 distinct bonds, exactly two rows per bond, and every row has its mirror row in the opposite direction
validation_method: cardinality and mirror-row check over the connectivity relation

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT MIN(atom_id, atom_id2), MAX(atom_id, atom_id2), bond_id FROM connected)
result: 12379 distinct undirected atom pairs, exactly one pair per bond, so the connectivity relation resolves each bond into its two constituent atoms
validation_method: distinct unordered pair count compared with the bond count

query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE a.element IN ('i','s'); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT atom_id FROM connected GROUP BY atom_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
result: 293 connectivity rows versus 119 distinct atoms for the iodine and sulfur populations, and 5745 atoms occupy more than one connectivity row, so row counts exceed atom counts
validation_method: row count compared with distinct atom count over a filtered connectivity join

query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) FROM atom
result: 12333 atom rows spanning 444 molecules, with no null element and no null molecule reference
validation_method: cardinality and null check over the atom relation

query: SELECT bond_id, molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_id IN ('TR001_6_9','TR001_10_11'); SELECT atom_id, element FROM atom WHERE atom_id IN ('TR001_6','TR001_9','TR001_10','TR001_11')
result: bond TR001_6_9 belongs to molecule TR001 and bond TR001_10_11 belongs to molecule TR001; atoms TR001_6, TR001_9, TR001_10 and TR001_11 all exist, confirming that a bond identifier composes its molecule prefix with the positions of the two atoms it links
validation_method: identifier decomposition checked against existing atom and molecule identifiers

query: SELECT SUM(element = 'h'), COUNT(*) FROM atom WHERE molecule_id = 'TR006'
result: molecule TR006 holds 17 hydrogen atoms out of 47 atoms, a share of 0.3617 of its atoms
validation_method: within-molecule element count compared with the molecule atom total

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom WHERE element = 'i'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM connected WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'i')
result: 6 iodine atoms, which account for 6 connectivity rows anchored on them, so the mean bond incidences per iodine atom is 1
validation_method: population count compared with its connectivity rows

query: SELECT m.label, COUNT(*) FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE a.element = 'h' GROUP BY m.label
result: hydrogen atoms resolve to 1569 atoms in carcinogenic molecules and 2465 atoms in non-carcinogenic molecules, showing that an element population is partitioned by the label of its molecule
validation_method: join between atom element population and molecule classification
